title: Atonement for Unknown Murder
english: When a murder has been committed and the perpetrator is unknown, the elders of the city must bring a heifer down to a rugged ravine that has not been worked or sown, a place where no one has ever labored or planted anything.

There, they will strike the heifer's neck, and the priests and Levites will approach, for they have been chosen by the Lord to stand before Him and bless in His name, and according to their word, every dispute and every assault will be resolved.

The elders will then wash their hands over the head of the beheaded heifer and declare that they did not shed the blood and did not see the crime, saying: 'Our hands did not shed this blood; and our eyes did not see' (Deuteronomy 21:7-8).

They will ask the Lord to be merciful to His people Israel, whom He redeemed from Egypt, and to remove the innocent blood from them, so that innocent blood may not be in His people Israel, and they will be atoned for the blood.
The Lord will atone for the blood, and they will be atoned for the blood, but He will remove the innocent blood from them if they do what is good and pleasing before the Lord their God.
Emmanuel was wounded for us, for he was bruised because of our sins, according to the Scriptures (Isaiah 53:5).
This was found to have happened in the land of the Jews, and outside the gate of Jerusalem; however, they did not know the one who struck, how or in what way.

Although we say the deeds against Christ are the work of the Jews' lawlessness, for they brought him to Pilate and cried out to crucify him, saying: 'Crucify him, crucify him' (Luke 23:21), and again: 'If you do not kill him, you are not a friend of Caesar' (John 19:12).

The divinely-inspired disciples of the Jewish leaders' obstinacy accused God openly, saying that the people had gathered in the city to condemn Jesus Christ, whom God had anointed, saying: 'For they gathered in truth in this city against your holy servant Jesus Christ, whom you anointed' (Acts 4:27).

The blessed Peter struck at the heart of the Jewish people, telling them that they had killed the author of life and denied the holy and righteous one, instead asking for a murderer to be released to them, saying: 'You killed the author of life' (Acts 3:15) and 'You denied the holy and righteous one and asked for a murderer to be granted to you' (Acts 3:14).

The law says that they do not know the one who struck, but this is a mystical word, not simply laid before everyone, but perhaps known only to those who understand the mystery of Christ correctly, and it is related to every dispute and every assault.

The teachers of the Jews and those who shared in their wicked schemes thought they had prevailed, but they did not realize that Christ suffered willingly, following the will of the Father and giving himself for us, and that He gave Himself up for us.
Jesus even told Pilate that he would have had no authority over him if it had not been given to him, saying: 'You would have had no authority over me if it had not been given to you' (John 19:11).

title: Attachment to the World
english: As we journey through life, we are borne by a power that improves our existence, leading us to a better life. The path to virtue is unwavering, yet the road that leads to base things is smooth, making it easy to stray.

The law provides guidance, stating that one should mourn the father and mother for a month of days, which means that it does not immediately make one's own home a delight, but rather briefly remembers those at home.

This phenomenon occurs when people are taken captive, even if they are treated with honor and allowed to indulge in luxury, they still long for their home and their own city, and are not less mindful of their own things. The Hebrews, who were redeemed from Egypt and from bitter slavery, called by God to the freedom that was theirs from above and from their fathers, still remembered Egypt and wept, saying they wished they had died in Egypt.
They reproached Moses, saying he had brought them out to the wilderness, demonstrating the strong attachment to the familiar and the worldly life.

It is necessary for those who have suffered afflictions to let go of them, because they have not yet acquired patience. This is evident in the way God condescended to the passion in the wilderness, showing mercy to the synagogue of the Jews and not utterly destroying the sinners, even though he was rightly angry.
By giving us a short time to mourn, God shows us that we are to receive the memories of our ancient intimacy with the world.
The divine Melodist also speaks to the church from the nations, saying: 'Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear, and forget your people and the house of your father.' (Song of Solomon 4:8)
This is a call to spiritual union, where the one who is joined to the Lord is one spirit.
Having mourned the father and mother for a month of days, we are then joined to God, and we become his wife. This is the promise of spiritual union, where we are one with God.

title: Spiritual Sacrifice
english: As we consider the stones, we are reminded of those who have believed in holy Christ and have been richly endowed with grace through holy baptism.
These individuals, who have crossed the Jordan, raise up for themselves teachers and mystagogues, the disciples of our Savior, the truly holy and chosen stones.
A prophetic word was spoken to us: For holy stones are rolled upon the earth.

The divine disciples, having been sent out into the world, proclaimed the beauty of their piety and the true pearl, which is Christ, the precious cornerstone, and they circled the world, showing to all the beauty of their piety and proclaiming the true pearl, the one and precious stone, that is, Christ.

The stones, having been anointed, have the law clearly written on them, and in the holy apostles, we find the theories of the law clearly and openly, no longer shaded by the letter, nor having a faint covering of shadow, but bright and pure, for the education of the holy ones is spiritual.
The holy ones speak the law clearly, inscribing it on the anointed stones, according to what is written.

When the stones on which the law was written are taken away, it is necessary to show a new altar made of other whole stones, that is, unblemished and not injured by iron blows, and these stones are unblemished.

Christ is the precious cornerstone, and he is also placed in the foundations of Zion, for we have been established under him, and having taken him as a firm and unshakeable foundation, we are living stones being built into a spiritual house, a holy temple, where God dwells in spirit.
This spiritual union is not unlike an altar, where we offer the fragrances of our virtues to God through our faith in Christ, and we are whole and unbroken, like stones.

Our minds are a whole burnt offering to God, undivided and single-minded, for as Christ is undivided, so we are single-minded and truthful, devoted to God alone, refusing to be divided towards fleshly and worldly things.
Paul, the divine messenger, writes to us, urging us to present our bodies as a living, holy, and pleasing sacrifice to God, which is our rational worship (Romans 12:1).

To live is Christ, and to die is gain (Philippians 1:21), and this means that we are devoted to God alone, refusing to be divided towards fleshly and worldly things, and instead, we offer ourselves to Him as a fragrant offering.
